title: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free [@ fetch_add] with WRITE of size 8
body:
Testcase found while fuzzing mozilla-central rev 5eb81f0156a8 (built with: --enable-address-sanitizer --enable-fuzzing).

Testcase can be reproduced using the following commands:
```
$ pip install fuzzfetch grizzly-framework
$ python -m fuzzfetch --build 5eb81f0156a8 --asan --fuzzing -n firefox
$ python -m grizzly.replay ./firefox/firefox testcase.html
```

So I think the plan here is:
1. We hold the WorkerPrivate alive with a strong ref through [the call to Write](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/00ea1649b59d5f427979e2d6ba42be96f62d6e82/dom/workers/Worker.cpp#146), which can absolutely call into content per reality and the spec, although this makes me sad and I am happy every time I forget this for a moment and sad every time I remember.
   - Strictly speaking we may not actually need to keep the WorkerPrivate alive here since we can check for `!mWorkerPrivate` after the call to Write and nothing but what is in our Worker::PostMessage call should have a way to access the Worker, but I would argue that it's good hygiene and makes us more resilient to any WorkerPrivate-referencing state that could exist in the MessageEventRunnable (because the MessageEventRunnable will be destroyed prior to us dropping the strong WorkerPrivate reference we acquire before its creation).  This is arguably desirable because the runnable's mWorkerPrivate is a stale reference to a freed object otherwise.
2. We check if the Worker is no longer in the running state after [the call to Write](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/00ea1649b59d5f427979e2d6ba42be96f62d6e82/dom/workers/Worker.cpp#146), and if so we do not dispatch the runnable.

I will do this.

(Edit: Write and read analyses completed.)

(In reply to Andrew Sutherland [:asuth] (he/him) from comment #13)
> The fix is up and I'll begin my audit of similar code paths shortly.

General context for the uniqueness of the worker situation (building on comment 10):
- The problem case on this bug involves dispatching a runnable to a worker which requires access to a valid WorkerPrivate because dispatch to a worker (currently) requires the runnable to be wrapped if it is not already, as well as to do book-keeping related to the dispatch that involves the WorkerPrivate.  This also involves a (conceptually) borrowed strong-reference which cannot survive a spun nested event loop that processes main thread runnables.

### Structured Serialization Write uses via StructuredCloneHolderBase

- [StructuredCloneHolderBase::Write(4-arg)](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/dom/base/StructuredCloneHolder.cpp#266)
  - [ConsoleRunnable::WriteData](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/dom/console/Console.cpp#443)
    - These are written to from a worker or worklet thread and so lifecycle concerns are not a problem.
- [StructuredCloneHolderBase::Write(2-arg)](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/dom/base/StructuredCloneHolder.cpp#261) calls SCHB:W(4-arg)
  - [PromiseWorkerProxy::RunCallback](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/dom/promise/Promise.cpp#906)
    - **Sketchy but fine, probably needs a spin-off for cleanups if we can't get rid of the class.**: This method obtains and holds a lock before the call to Write.  This is good because although the PromiseWorkerProxy holds a StrongWorkerRef, [it tries to drop it in its CleanUp method](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/dom/promise/Promise.cpp#949) which [gets called by the lambda callback passed to the StrongWorkerRef](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/dom/promise/Promise.cpp#839).  In a pathological case, this will hang the worker and prevent it from shutting down and creating lifecycle problems.  But in practice this should not be a problem because the code running on the main thread is system C++ code that is largely not using `Promise::AppendNativeHandler`.  The one exception is that [the ExtensionAPIRequestForwarder uses PromiseWorkerProxy](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionAPIRequestForwarder.cpp#342) and [uses AppendNativeHandler](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionAPIRequestForwarder.cpp#572) with it, but as discussed elsewhere in this analysis, that JS global is entirely system logic.  **I think this should be spun off** noting that [there aren't that many users PromiseWorkerProxy](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/search?q=PromiseWorkerProxy%3A%3ACreate&path=&case=false&regexp=false) so we shouldn't rule out eliminating usages of this class, although that may not be feasible.
      - Note that https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D173850 involves some discussion of PromiseWorkerProxy as it relates to WorkerFetchResolver.
  - [xpc::StackScopedClone](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/js/xpconnect/src/ExportHelpers.cpp#209) uses this to perform an immediate clone of something, optionally with an immediate deep freeze.
    - [Promise::MaybeResolveWithClone uses this](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/dom/promise/Promise.cpp#750) as [does MaybeRejectWithClone](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/dom/promise/Promise.cpp#766).
      - [PeerConnectionImpl::Operation::ResolvedCallback uses MaybeResolveWithClone](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/dom/media/webrtc/jsapi/PeerConnectionImpl.cpp#1238) and similar code for the rejection.
        - Probably not a concern.  It seems like bug 1624989 moved the code from potentially involving JS-implementation logic to having it all be C++, so this should be doubly moot because the JS code was system JS code in `PeerConnection.jsm`, but now it should be C++?
      - [Localization's PromiseResolve::ResolveCallback and PromiseResolve::RejectedCallback (which lack nice C++ namespaces)](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/intl/l10n/Localization.cpp#482,488).  This happens if [Localization::MaybeWrapPromise](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/search?q=symbol:_ZN7mozilla4intl12Localization16MaybeWrapPromiseEPNS_3dom7PromiseE&redirect=false) is used.
        - Not a concern.  The wrapping only is used against [FFI calls into rust](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/intl/l10n/Localization.cpp#270,285,297,314,326,349).
      - [ElementTranslationHandler's RejectedCallback uses the rejection case](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/dom/l10n/DOMLocalization.cpp#264).
        - Not a concernm, this only seems to be used for the `IsChromeOrUAWidget`-checked [DOMLocalization.webidl](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/webidl/DOMLocalization.webidl) which is explicitly chrome or in a private compartment and like the above is [just calling through to rust code](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/intl/l10n/Localization.cpp#317,326,349).
    - [xpc::CloneInto uses this](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/js/xpconnect/src/XPCComponents.cpp#2323) and in turn
    [SandboxCloneInto uses xpc::CloneInto](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/js/xpconnect/src/Sandbox.cpp#482) which is then [conditionally exposed to sandboxes as "cloneInto" if wantExportHelpers was passed](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/1157486abdf3245c2d3bf425745314c090745de5/js/xpconnect/src/Sandbox.cpp#1465).
      - This is all system code on the system principal side of any membranes.
- [StructuredCloneHolder::Write(5-arg)](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/af78418c4b5f2c8721d1a06486cf4cf0b33e1e8d/dom/base/StructuredCloneHolder.cpp#359) callers:
  - [dom/base/ PostMessageEvent::Write](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/af78418c4b5f2c8721d1a06486cf4cf0b33e1e8d/dom/base/PostMessageEvent.h#70) called [from nsGlobalWindowOuter::PostMessageMozOuter](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/dom/base/nsGlobalWindowOuter.cpp#5968)
    - Not a concern.  The Event is strongly held.  The dispatch gets a little involved and I didn't dig too deeply into this, but in general on the main thread we don't have lifecycle problems with too few window strong refs.
  - [AudioWorkletNode::Constructor](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/af78418c4b5f2c8721d1a06486cf4cf0b33e1e8d/dom/media/webaudio/AudioWorkletNode.cpp#779) serializes an [AudioWorkletNodeOptions webidl dict](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/dom/webidl/AudioWorkletNode.webidl#14-20) which can contain arbitrary data but forbids transferring (which excludes streams).
    - Not a concern.  The AudioWorkletNode is strongly held (and not yet exposed to content), plus the binding is holding all the rest of the args.
  - [Worker::PostMessage](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/af78418c4b5f2c8721d1a06486cf4cf0b33e1e8d/dom/workers/Worker.cpp#146)
    - (This case that we are already fixing.)
  - [WorkerPrivate::PostMessageToParent](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/af78418c4b5f2c8721d1a06486cf4cf0b33e1e8d/dom/workers/WorkerPrivate.cpp#4613)
    - Not a concern.  This is happening on a worker thread where the WorkerPrivate's self-ref inherently cannot be freed until the stack is cleared all the way back to the primary runnable.  Additionally, worker syncloops are less ill-conceived than main-thread syncloops because they have their own nested event queue.
- [StructuredCloneHolder::Write(3-arg)](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/af78418c4b5f2c8721d1a06486cf4cf0b33e1e8d/dom/base/StructuredCloneHolder.cpp#354) calls 5-arg, and has callers:
  - [SerializedStackHolder::WriteStack](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/dom/base/SerializedStackHolder.cpp#27) has 2 variations:
    - [SerializedStackHolder::SerializeWorkerStack](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/dom/base/SerializedStackHolder.cpp#53)
      - Not a concern.  Happens on the worker and holds a StrongWorkerRef throughout the call to boot.  (Not necessary for the Write call, but is used for the use case.)
    - [SerializedStackHolder::SerializeMainThreadOrWorkletStack](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/dom/base/SerializedStackHolder.cpp#33)
      - Not a concern.  Although we can be on the main thread, we're dealing with rooted values which relate to the current main-thread global in that case.  In the worklet case it should not be possible to spin an event loop.
  - [StructuredCloneBlob::Constructor](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/dom/base/StructuredCloneBlob.cpp#79) as exposed by [the chrome-webidl StructuredCloneHolder](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/chrome-webidl/StructuredCloneHolder.webidl) which is `Exposed=(Window,Worker)` so this will happen on the main thread and on workers.
    - Not a concern.  The holder has a strong ref for the duration and this is directly binding exposed so there's no extra C++ stuff happening in the call stack.
  - [ClonedErrorHolder::Init](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/dom/ipc/ClonedErrorHolder.cpp#124) (which has a [good commit message](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D50881) but not a good comment; it's to allow serializing Errors, although https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4268 and friends actually made this possible in the spec prior to that patch).
    - Not a concern.  The write pattern is into a data structure with no subsequent actions in the immediate vicinity.  There is [a bit going on in the call graph](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/query/default?q=calls-to%3A%27mozilla%3A%3Adom%3A%3AClonedErrorHolder%3A%3AInit%27%20depth%3A4) but they are commonly in native promise resolve/reject handlers which means the native stack should be short.  Additionally, I think the value domain is intentionally limited.
  - [WorkletModuleLoader::OnModuleLoadComplete](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/dom/worklet/loader/WorkletModuleLoader.cpp#246) on the worklet thread where it creates an [AddModuleThrowErrorRunnable thin StructuredCloneHolder/Runnable hybrid subclass](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/dom/worklet/loader/WorkletModuleLoader.cpp#162).
    - Not a concern.  The worklet doesn't spin event loops and the runnable isn't dispatched until after the write completes.
  - ExtensionAPIRequestForwarder [RequestWorkerRunnable::SerializeArgs](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionAPIRequestForwarder.cpp#391) whose class has a [nice doc block](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionAPIRequestForwarder.h#107-123).
    - Not a concern because this is happening on the worker (and the sync runnable is good about checking the rv from the syncloop dispatch).
  - ExtensionAPIRequestForwarder [RequestWorkerRunnable::ProcessHandlerResult](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionAPIRequestForwarder.cpp#590) where this is the main-thread counterpart to the above, serializing the returned value or error.
    - Not a concern.  A major note is that this is proxied extension system code, not extension code or content code, and is not expected to be hostile, but also in general even if it was, there isn't anything lifecycle-concern wise here.  Note that this code overlaps with the PromiseWorkerProxy scenario mentioned above; that case handles calls which return a promise whereas I believe this case processes synchronously available results.
  - [ExtensionEventListener::SerializeCallArguments](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionEventListener.cpp#205) is the other direction, going from main-thread to the extension worker.
    - **Theoretical, but non-exploitable concern interacting with a lock handling bug.** Not exploitable because 1) it's all system code and 2) a lock is being held through the write call that should not be held through the write call, but which provides protection against the ThreadSafeWorkerRef from being dropped during the critical time between the write call and the subsequent dispatch call.  A nefarious attacker's attempt to exploit would result in deadlock if they could get control over the webext main thread global, but I don't think they can.  **I think it's best to spin this one off.**
      - The pattern used [in the call to SerializeCallArguments followed by the creation of the ExtensionListenerCallWorkerRunnable](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionEventListener.cpp#298-307) has the same shape as on this bug, but the lock that manages mWorkerRef [is acquired earlier in the method and mWorkerRef explicitly checked](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionEventListener.cpp#275).  In general it's not correct to hold the lock through the call to write because of the call into content that can happen, but it is protecting the bad thing from happening here.
      - (With the lock held), After serializing into the argsHolder, an [ExtensionListenerCallWorkerRunnable](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionEventListener.h#121) is created which is a WorkerRunnable sub-class and pulls a WorkerPrivate raw pointer ref from [ExtensionEventListener::GetWorkerPrivate](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionEventListener.cpp#313).  That comes from its [ThreadSafeWorkerRef mWorkerRef](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionEventListener.h#105) which generally provides the safety we want, as long as it can't be dropped.  (And the mutex currently does provide that protection.)
      - Looking at the [call graph leading to ExtensionEventListener::Cleanup](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/query/default?q=calls-to%3A%27mozilla%3A%3Aextensions%3A%3AExtensionEventListener%3A%3ACleanup%27%20depth%3A4) where the worker ref is dropped (and thereby allows the worker to shutdown), ExtensionEventManager::AddListener [does have a lambda that calls ReleaseListeners which can trigger the worker ref to be dropped](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionEventManager.cpp#98-100).  That lambda is moved into [the StrongWorkerRef created by ExtensionEventListener::Create on the worker thread](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionEventListener.cpp#176-177).  But [the cleanup call tries to acquire the lock](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionEventListener.h#74-79), so if there was nefarious code, the worker would stall at this point until the runnable on the main thread is dispatched.  This could also effectively lead to deadlock if the nefarious main thread code refused to yield control like because it was waiting for a web lock to be released.
  - [ExtensionListenerCallPromiseResultHandler::WorkerRunCallback](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5349e0db4db34dabecced362a59ea7528dcc7afc/toolkit/components/extensions/webidl-api/ExtensionEventListener.cpp#621) is again the flip side of the above.  It is running on the worker thread and we can also see the use of the ClonedErrorHolder above the call to wrap the error.
    - Not a concern.  This is on the worker so syncloops aren't a problem.  (Also, although this involves web-ext provided JS, the code is being called as part of a resolve/reject handler so the stack is also boring at this point.)
- [StructuredCloneData::Write(5-arg)](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/af78418c4b5f2c8721d1a06486cf4cf0b33e1e8d/dom/ipc/StructuredCloneData.cpp#128) calls SCH:W(5-arg), and has callers:
  - [BrowsingContext::PostMessageMoz](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/docshell/base/BrowsingContext.cpp#2391)
    - Not a concern, no lifetime concerns for the window or browsing contexts.
  - [nsFrameMessageManager::GetParamsForMessage](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/base/nsFrameMessageManager.cpp#445)
    - Not a concern, this is all internal system messaging.
  - [Client::PostMessage](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/clients/api/Client.cpp#101)
    - Not a concern.  This is explicitly worker-exposed only at this time, which means there are no worker lifetime concerns.  And `mHandle` is never cleared and will be initialized before use.
  - [SharedMessageBody::Write](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/ipc/SharedMessageBody.cpp#50) is called by:
    - [BroadcastChannel::PostMessage](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/broadcastchannel/BroadcastChannel.cpp#285)
    - [MessagePort::PostMessage](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/messagechannel/MessagePort.cpp#351)
    - **Only nullptr deref concern if it's possible to initiate a navigation from inside the syncloop that triggers DETH disconnects.**  Both APIs operate over IPC so there are no thread coordination concerns.  Both are DETHs and care about being detached and they will clear out `mActor` which is blindly accessed following the call to write, so if the serialization is able to trigger [nsGlobalWindowOuter::SetNewDocument to call FreeInnerObjects](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/base/nsGlobalWindowOuter.cpp#2474) because [doomCurrentInner was set to true because the window wasn't being put in the bfcache](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/base/nsGlobalWindowOuter.cpp#2273) then we can end up dereferencing a nullptr.  **Probably want a spin-off to validate whether we can get to FreeInnerObjects in this case and if so fix these to check if they've been detached during the serialization.**  I don't think we would want to add the null checks in this bug because it would be quite explicit.
  - [ServiceWorker::PostMessage](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/ipc/SharedMessageBody.cpp#50)
    - Not a concern.  Conceptually similar to the BroadcastChannel/MessagePort situation except the logic already has a check for `!mActor` after the write and before the call, so it's protected against that hypothetical.  But it also does not discard the actor during `DisconnectFromOwner`; instead it waits to drop the actor until the ServiceWorker binding is destroyed, which probably means it waits until GC.
- [StructuredCloneData::Write(3-arg)](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/af78418c4b5f2c8721d1a06486cf4cf0b33e1e8d/dom/ipc/StructuredCloneData.cpp#119) calls SCD:W(5-arg), and has callers
  - Not a concern.  There's a bunch of these, but they're all definitely internal system code not subject to concerning usage patterns.
- [nsContentUtils::StructuredClone](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/af78418c4b5f2c8721d1a06486cf4cf0b33e1e8d/dom/base/nsContentUtils.cpp#10090) calls SCH:W(5-arg), exposes a method to perform a clone in a given global via write/read pair and has callers:
  - [nsGlobalWindowInner::StructuredClone](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/base/nsGlobalWindowInner.cpp#7641) which exposes the algorithm to content per spec
    - Not a concern.  Just calls the method, does nothing extra before returning.
  - [WorkerGlobalScope::StructuredClone](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/workers/WorkerScope.cpp#797) also exposes the algorithm to content per spec
    - Not a concern.  Just calls the method, does nothing extra before returning.
  - [SandboxStructuredClone exposed as "structuredClone" in sandboxes](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/js/xpconnect/src/Sandbox.cpp#388)
    - Not a concern.  Just calls the method, does nothing extra before returning although it involves more JS boilerplate than the above cases.
  - [Performance::Measure](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/performance/Performance.cpp#633) clones the [measureOptions.detail field per spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Performance/measure)
    - Not a concern.  The operation is same-global.
  - [PerformanceMark::Constructor](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e941c8a6d49b4f62f361446de7a80214fb899186/dom/performance/PerformanceMark.cpp#76) via the constructor or `performance.mark()`.
    - Fine, same-global, even less happens than the measure case, the mark just gets returned.

### Structured Serialization Read uses via StructuredCloneHolderBase

I audited these as well, and there didn't seem to be any extra cases.  Note that
many of the write cases above were inherently paired with a read case that I had
already analyzed.

Created attachment 9323332
repro-100.html

Oh no, I missed an important point from the repro code, uploading a new repro that reproduces 100%.

* `highWaterMark: 0` ensures no pull happens before transfer, because doing so will cause piping to wait for the pull to finish (which is why the the current repro only happens intermittently).
* `await Promise.resolve()` is to make sure the start algorithm finishes, because piping will also wait if not.

The point is that piping can synchronously pull, as you already noted. Well, unfortunately this is the reality currently. The following emits "before transfer", "pull", "after transfer" on both Gecko and Blink (while Safari simply doesn't support stream transfer)

```js
r = new ReadableStream({ pull(c) { console.log('pull') } }, { highWaterMark: 0 })
await Promise.resolve();
console.log('before transfer')
structuredClone([r], { transfer: [r] }); console.log('after transfer')
```
